content.en: Artificial intelligence (AI) is playing an increasingly important role in orthopaedic surgery. It improves patient care by aiding in diagnosis, management, research, and systems analysis. AI and machine learning (ML) advancements are being used for clinical diagnosis, predicting post-operative outcomes, and complications in orthopaedic surgery. AI-based computational algorithms can also predict injury risk, interpret advanced imaging, evaluate patient-reported outcomes, and enhance telehealth. AI has extensive potential clinical applications in the surgical setting and is gradually changing surgery through advanced technological development in imaging, navigation, and robotic intervention. It can personalize risk prediction, detect implant specifics, and monitor patient movement and recovery in orthopaedic surgery. However, data quality is crucial for the success of machine learning applications. AI has the potential to augment surgeons by providing decision support, assessing technical skills, and performing tasks in surgery. German surgeons are positively disposed toward AI applications, but there is a deficit in knowledge and implementation in their professional environment. AI is also being investigated to optimize clinical efficiency in various subfields of plastic and reconstructive surgery. While AI has the potential to reduce cognitive load and support human performance in surgery, accurate and reliable systems require surgeon involvement. AI is used for diagnostics, predictive models, rehabilitation monitoring, and surgical training in orthopaedic surgery. However, the state-of-the-art of AI-enabled decision support in surgery is limited by small sample sizes, lack of external validation, and inadequate reporting. Sudanese orthopaedic surgeons are aware of AI applications but have doubts about safety and are interested in utilizing AI in various aspects of surgery. Orthopaedic patients are generally comfortable with AI joining the care team, but their knowledge and experience with AI impact their perspectives. Trauma and emergency surgeons have varying opinions on AI-based tools, with some believing in their potential and others expressing mistrust. Surgeons should consider ethical considerations such as patient safety, autonomy, confidentiality, informed consent, and surgical training in AI-assisted robotic surgery when adopting emerging innovations in AI and robotics.
content.da: Kunstig intelligens (AI) spiller en stadig vigtigere rolle i ortopædisk kirurgi. Det forbedrer patientplejen ved at hjælpe med diagnosticering, styring, forskning og systemanalyse. Fremskridt inden for AI og machine learning (ML) anvendes til klinisk diagnose, forudsigelse af post-operative resultater og komplikationer i ortopædisk kirurgi. AI-baserede beregningsalgoritmer kan også forudsige skaderisiko, fortolke avanceret billedbehandling, evaluere patientrapporterede resultater og forbedre telemedicin. AI har omfattende potentielle kliniske anvendelser i det kirurgiske miljø og ændrer gradvist kirurgi gennem avanceret teknologisk udvikling inden for billedbehandling, navigation og robotintervention. Det kan tilpasse risikoprædiktion, registrere implantatspecifikationer og overvåge patienters bevægelse og bedring i ortopædisk kirurgi. Dog er datakvalitet afgørende for succesen af machine learning-applikationer. AI har potentiale til at supplere kirurger ved at tilbyde beslutningsstøtte, vurdere tekniske færdigheder og udføre opgaver i kirurgi. Tyske kirurger er positivt indstillede over for AI-applikationer, men der er et videns- og implementeringsdeficit i deres professionelle miljø. AI undersøgelse også for at optimere klinisk effektivitet inden for forskellige underområder af plastikkirurgi og rekonstruktiv kirurgi. Mens AI har potentiale til at reducere kognitiv belastning og støtte menneskelig præstation i kirurgi, kræver præcise og pålidelige systemer involvering fra kirurger. AI anvendes til diagnoser, prædiktive modeller, rehabiliteringsovervågning og kirurgisk træning i ortopædisk kirurgi. Men den nuværende status for AI-aktiveret beslutningsstøtte i kirurgi er begrænset af små stikprøvestørrelser, mangel på ekstern validering og utilstrækkelig rapportering. Sudanske ortopædkirurger er klar over AI-applikationer, men har tvivl om sikkerhed og er interesserede i at udnytte AI i forskellige aspekter af kirurgi. Ortopædiske patienter er generelt komfortable med, at AI bliver en del af plejeteamet, men deres viden og erfaring med AI påvirker deres perspektiver. Traume- og akutkirurger har forskellige meninger om AI-baserede værktøjer, hvor nogle tror på deres potentiale, mens andre udtrykker mistillid. Kirurger bør overveje etiske overvejelser som patientsikkerhed, autonomi, fortrolighed, informeret samtykke og kirurgisk træning i AI-assisteret robotkirurgi, når de adopterer nye innovationer inden for AI og robotteknologi.

critic.en: Oh, the joy of having AI involved in yet another intricate human skill! How reassuring it is that so many of us are enthusiastically placing our faith in the hands of algorithms and machines. But here's a question: if AI starts to make decisions that directly impact patient outcomes, should we hold it accountable like we do with human surgeons? Or is this just another instance where technology operates in a moral gray area?
critic.da: Forestil dig en fremtid, hvor vi overlader vores kropslige integritet til systemer, der kan være lige så fejlbarlige som os selv. Vil du hellere opereres af en maskine, fordi den kan "forudsige" komplikationer, eller vil du have en erfaren kirurg, der forstår den menneskelige kompleksitet? Jeg mener, at vi risikerer at tabe noget helt fundamentalt, når vi søger at erstatte menneskelig intuition og erfaring med algoritmer.

potential.en: I applaud the integration of AI into orthopaedic surgery as it can lead to more personalized care and enhanced decision-making for both patients and clinicians. The potential of AI and machine learning in predicting outcomes and complications in orthopaedic surgery is impressive. The gradual change in the surgical setting through advanced technology, imaging, and robotic interventions is an exciting development. I believe the use of AI in monitoring patient movement and recovery can significantly benefit orthopaedic surgery. It's great to see German surgeons being open to AI applications, although more efforts are needed in knowledge and implementation. AI's involvement in plastic and reconstructive surgery is also promising. Surgeons recognizing the importance of AI and being involved in its development is crucial in creating accurate and reliable AI systems for surgery. The positive awareness of Sudanese orthopaedic surgeons about AI applications is a good start, and addressing their safety concerns is essential. Input from trauma and emergency surgeons on AI-based tools will be valuable in further advancements. Ethical considerations must always be at the forefront when adopting AI and robotic innovations to ensure patient safety and maintain trust. Overall, the potential of AI in orthopaedic surgery is vast, and I am optimistic about the future of this integration.
potential.da: AI i ortopædisk kirurgi åbner døren til en ny æra, hvor patientpleje kan forbedres markant. Det er fascinerende at se, hvordan AI kan hjælpe med alt fra diagnoser til forudsigelser om komplikationer. Mange kirurger, især i Tyskland, er positive overfor AI, men der er stadig en mangel på viden og implementering. Det er vigtigt, at vi uddanner og inddrager kirurgerne, så vi kan udnytte AI's potentiale fuldt ud. Hvorfor tror du, at nogle kirurger stadig er skeptiske overfor AI i kirurgien?
